# Gāmaṇijātaka (Ja 8)

**ID:** Ja 8
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)

**Title (Pali):** Gāmaṇijātaka

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

It begins with the verse opening *Api ataramānānaṃ* and is set in Jetavana [Fausböll 1877]. According to its introductory framework (*paccuppannavatthu*), the Buddha delivered the discourse concerning a monk who had slackened his effort or given up striving (*ossatthaviriya*) [Fausböll 1877].

As noted by the commentary, both the present occasion and the story of the past (*atītavatthu*) share their core narrative with the *Saṃvarajātaka* found in the eleventh book (*Ekādasanipāta*), differing primarily in their verses [Fausböll 1877]. In the narrative, Prince Gāmaṇi heeds the counsel of the Bodhisatta, surpasses his one hundred elder brothers to obtain kingship, and utters an exultant utterance (*udāna*) regarding how relying on his teacher enabled him to secure the realm; upon hearing the teaching, the despondent monk attained arahantship [Fausböll 1877].
